record.paper_title: Open problems from the 12th International Conference on Fuzzy Set Theory and Its Applications
record.original_question: Determine for which classes of semicopulas S, and possibly for which classes of capacities, strict convergence in measure is equivalent to convergence in mean defined by the smallest semicopula-based universal integral I_S.

evidence.quote: Problem 9.5 (O. Hutnik). For which class of semicopulas (of capacities, eventually) is strict convergence in measure equivalent to mean convergence?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Setup. A semicopula is a function S:[0,1]×[0,1]→[0,1] that is non-decreasing in each argument and satisfies S(1,x)=S(x,1)=x for all x∈[0,1]. Let (X,𝓐) be a measurable space. A capacity (monotone measure) on (X,𝓐) is a set function m:𝓐→[0,∞] with m(∅)=0 and m(A)≤m(B) whenever A⊆B. For a measurable function f:X→[0,∞) and a capacity m, the smallest semicopula-based universal integral is defined by
   I_S(m,f) = sup_{t>0} S( t, m({f≥t}) ).

Convergences. Let (f_n) be a sequence of 𝓐-measurable nonnegative functions and let f be such a function.
 • (f_n) converges in measure to f if for every ε>0, m({|f_n−f|≥ε}) → 0 as n→∞.
 • (f_n) converges strictly in measure to f if (f_n) converges in measure to f and, in addition, m({|f_n−f|≥ε}) = 0 for all sufficiently large n and every ε>0 outside a null set of thresholds (i.e. the stronger notion in which convergence in measure is accompanied by m({|f_n−f|≥ε})→0 uniformly in the standard "strict" sense used for semicopula-based integrals).
 • (f_n) converges in mean (with respect to I_S and m) to f if I_S(m, |f_n−f|) → 0 as n→∞.

Problem. Characterize all classes of semicopulas S (and, possibly, all classes of capacities m) for which strict convergence in measure of (f_n) to f is equivalent to convergence of (f_n) to f in mean defined by the smallest semicopula-based universal integral I_S.
artifact.status_search_result: Recent works (2023–2025) by Hutník and collaborators on almost-uniform convergence theorems and improvements on convergence in measure for semicopula-based universal integrals have produced partial answers. In particular, results show that, under natural conditions, strict convergence in measure is equivalent to convergence in measure and to convergence in mean only in degenerate cases (e.g. when the underlying monotone measure is trivial), while sufficient conditions on the semicopula (continuity, trivial zero divisors) and on the capacity (autocontinuity) yield equivalences in several settings. A complete characterization of all classes of semicopulas and capacities for which the equivalence holds does not appear to be established.

status_evidence.title: The smallest semicopula-based universal integrals II: Convergence theorems
status_evidence.snippet: Convergence theorems for S-integral sequences including monotone, a.e., almost uniform, in measure and in mean.
status_evidence.claim: Provides convergence theorems and shows mean convergence does not in general imply strict convergence in measure.

status_evidence.title: On almost uniform convergence theorems for the smallest semicopula-based universal integral
status_evidence.snippet: Almost uniform convergence theorems for semicopula-based universal integrals.
status_evidence.claim: Provides additional partial conditions relating different convergence modes for I_S.

status_evidence.title: Some improvements on the convergence in measure for sequence of semicopula-based universal integrals
status_evidence.snippet: Improvements on convergence in measure for semicopula-based universal integrals.
status_evidence.claim: Recent improvements give partial answers to when convergence in measure (and strict) coincides with mean convergence.

status_evidence.title: Autocontinuity, strict convergence in measure and convergence of integral sequences
status_evidence.snippet: Autocontinuity and strict convergence in measure for integral sequences.
status_evidence.claim: Shows autocontinuity-type conditions on the capacity yield equivalence between strict convergence in measure and convergence of integral sequences.
